clips.text: The oldest cooking pot is twenty thousand years old.
A wet mud bowl slumps in water and falls back into the riverbank before dinner even starts.
But the fired pot holds its shape and steams over a cave fire while snow blows past the cave mouth.
It is the oldest known cooking pot, about twenty thousand years old.
That is about ten thousand years before anyone planted a field or kept a farm.
So why did a lump of river mud survive the fire twenty thousand years before farms?
Past about six hundred degrees, mud changes for good, bonds, and cannot melt back. Tap the video link under my name.
